 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham spoke to reporters at his weekly press conference on Monday.
 Whittingham was asked about the firing of former offensive coordinator Jason Beck on Sunday, but he also looked ahead to this weekend's game against Oregon.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Michigan head coach is apparently undecided on the starting quarterback, telling reporters it is "TBD" after the loss to Michigan State and the offensive coordinator change.
 Michigan has used both Bryce Underwood and true freshman Tommy Carr as its starting quarterback this season. Whittingham even said Carr would be the team's starting quarterback for the " foreseeable future " after his performance against Rutgers on Oct. 31.
 After Michigan lost 15-6 against Michigan State last Saturday, though, the head coach has changed his tune. Whittingham said Carr had a great game against Rutgers, but that the quarterback took a big drop-off against the Spartans. He added that Michigan needs better play from all its offensive units moving forward.
 Underwood began the season as the incumbent starter but started slowly as the Wolverines barely beat Western Michigan in a controversial Week 1 win , and then beat then-No. 11 Oklahoma 17-10.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The sophomore quarterback has seen action in seven of Michigan's games this year. Underwood has thrown for 924 yards, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions, and has added 222 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
 Underwood was benched at halftime of Michigan's Oct. 17 game against Penn State. Carr took over and led the Wolverines to a 21-18 win. After that, he started against Indiana, but Michigan lost 13-6 in overtime.
 Carr and the Wolverines bounced back with a 28-21 win over Rutgers, but then lost to Michigan State last weekend.
 The true freshman has played in five games and has thrown for 641 yards, 2 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Carr has added 95 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After the loss to Michigan State, Michigan is now 5-4 but 2-4 in Big Ten play this year.
 The Wolverines will take the road to face No. 23 Oregon this weekend, then end the season with games against undefeated No. 8 UCLA, followed by "The Game" on the road against No. 12 Ohio State.
